full_text:
**Verdict: KNOWN.** This is parallel (synchronous) chip-firing, also called the deterministic fixed-energy sandpile, run on an Erdős–Rényi graph and on small-world rewired rings. Confidence is medium-high. Your exact numbers are not tabulated anywhere I found, so the call rests on the model and the phenomenon being documented.

**1. Model family.** This is a conservative sandpile or chip-firing cellular automaton on graphs, with threshold equal to degree, no sink, and all active sites toppling at once. It is called the parallel chip-firing game or candy-passing game, and each vertex fires one chip to each neighbour when it can. In the physics literature it is the Bak–Tang–Wiesenfeld (BTW) fixed-energy sandpile. The BTW dynamics with parallel updating is completely deterministic and Abelian.

**2. Is the behaviour described?** Yes, piece by piece.

- **Origin of the model.** Bitar and Goles introduced it in 1992 as a special case of the Björner–Lovász–Shor chip-firing game of 1991. It always ends up periodic.
- **Onset of lasting activity and the activity-versus-density staircase.** Bagnoli, Cecconi, Flammini and Vespignani (EPL 63:512, 2003) studied the BTW fixed-energy sandpile on lattices. The system settles into limit cycles. Activity shows a devil's staircase against energy density, over a symmetric set of energy intervals where period lengths are also constant. That symmetry is the "mirrored rhythm reappears" feature. Levine's review (arXiv 1001.3401) notes that two mirror-image configurations stay mirror images after a parallel step.
- **Complete graph.** Levine, "Parallel chip-firing on the complete graph: Devil's staircase and Poincaré rotation number," Ergodic Theory Dynam. Systems 31 (2011), 891–910. It links the dynamics to the Poincaré rotation number of a circle map. Activity stays constant over long intervals and then jumps suddenly.
- **Erdős–Rényi graphs.** Kiss, Levine and Tóthmérész, "The devil's staircase for chip-firing on random graphs and on graphons," Random Structures & Algorithms 66, e21255 (2025); arXiv 2004.13104. It studies parallel chip-firing activity as chips are added on an Erdős–Rényi graph. The activity diagrams converge to a devil's staircase as the number of vertices grows. This is the closest match to your main system.
- **Random networks and rewiring, the physics counterpart.** Fazli and Azimi-Tafreshi, "Emergence of oscillations in fixed-energy sandpile models on complex networks," Phys. Rev. E 105, 014303 (2022); arXiv 2110.12760. Close to the absorbing transition, the density of active nodes oscillates and nodes topple in synchrony. They attribute this to the deterministic toppling rule and the small-world property. Oscillation amplitude grows with network randomness. This matches your finding of no rhythm on the unrewired ring and rhythm once links are rewired. I did not check whether their toppling threshold equals degree.
- **Top end, where nearly everything stays active.** Any parallel chip-firing game on a graph G with at least 4|E(G)| − |V(G)| chips stabilizes, with eventual period 1. I found no source for your rhythm-end value of about 13.96. It sits below that bound (about 19 here), and the bound only guarantees stabilization, so the two don't conflict.
- **Period-2 rung.** A recent arXiv paper (2608.04153) addresses games with 2|E|−|V| < |σ| < 2|E| chips, which it says have period 2. For mean degree 10 that is a density between 9 and 10. This brackets your two-level alternation onset (8.95) and your rhythm return (10.05) fairly well. That paper is a very recent preprint, so treat it as supporting rather than established. Levine's review also lists the cycle as having jumps at densities 1 and 2.

**3. Caveats on what differs.**
- Kiss et al. prove their staircase for dense Erdős–Rényi graphs. Your mean degree of 10 on 10,000 nodes is sparse, and the finite-size values (5.51, 8.95, 10.05, 13.96) are numerical details. The qualitative picture (onset, plateaus, mirror symmetry, jump to full activity) is standard.
- I did not verify exact published values for the onset density on Erdős–Rényi graphs or for the rewiring fraction at which rhythm appears. The threshold of 10% rewiring is a simulation number I could not match to a source.
- The "7 rule programs" are parameter variants of one model, not new rules.

**Citations checked against search results:** Bagnoli et al. (EPL 2003), Levine (ETDS 2011, arXiv 0811.2800), Kiss–Levine–Tóthmérész (RSA 2025), Fazli & Azimi-Tafreshi (PRE 2022), and Bitar & Goles (1992). I confirmed Bitar & Goles only through other papers' reference lists and descriptions, not the original.
